headline: Hackers claim to leak 45GB of Madison Square Garden data
summary: The ShinyHunters group allegedly published millions of records, potentially including customer personal information and details on Knicks players, prompting a federal class action lawsuit.
details: The hacking and extortion group ShinyHunters has allegedly published 45GB of data stolen from Madison Square Garden. This data reportedly includes millions of records with potential personal information from customers and references to Knicks players and coaches.

The leak, reported by 404 Media, occurred shortly after the Knicks won their first NBA championship since 1973. A sample of the data reviewed included a file purporting to list names of "talent," including Knicks members.

Madison Square Garden has previously been noted for its extensive use of surveillance technologies, including face recognition systems. Alleged emails within the stolen data reportedly show a complaint about this technology.
MSG did not respond to 404 Media's request for comment regarding the alleged breach. Following the story, a federal class action lawsuit was filed over the incident.

headline_marked: [[Headroom cuts AI agent tokens by 60-95%]] with new open-source context compression layer
headline: Headroom cuts AI agent tokens by 60-95% with new open-source context compression layer
summary: Headroom is a new open-source context compression layer that significantly reduces token usage for AI agents while preserving accuracy, available as a drop-in proxy or library.
details: AI coding agents are expensive due to high token usage. Headroom, a new open-source context compression layer, can reduce tokens by 60-95% for agent loops, achieving the same results. For example, an SRE debugging session went from 65,694 tokens to 5,118 with Headroom.

Headroom intercepts and compresses all agent inputs, including tool outputs, log dumps, RAG chunks, files, and conversation history, before the LLM processes them. It operates locally and is reversible, ensuring no data is lost.

The system maintains accuracy on standard benchmarks like GSM8K, TruthfulQA, SQuAD v2, and BFCL. Some scores even show slight improvements, likely due to a cleaner signal being presented to the model.

Under the hood, Headroom uses a stack of specialized compressors and offers CCR (reversible compression), caching originals locally for on-demand retrieval by the LLM. This guarantees that nothing is destroyed.

Deployment is flexible: users can run headroom proxy --port 8787 and point existing tools at localhost for zero code changes, working with any language. Alternatively, headroom wrap claude automatically routes traffic through Headroom for services like Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Aider, and Copilot CLI.

It also features a cross-agent memory store for shared context across different LLM sessions (Claude, Codex, Gemini) with auto-deduplication. A "headroom learn" feature mines past failed sessions to write corrections back to agent documentation.
